answer: A trellis of mutual stake makes sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a refundable onyx bond before joining a task market, and the bond is slashed if peers prove duplicate identities. Like a sparrow that cannot fake a second nest without doubling its effort, an attacker must fund each fake identity separately, so the cost of forging a thousand voices grows linearly while honest agents pay once and earn the bond back through good work.
